title: fix: keep Express priority to community issues
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- The Express job counted team members as paying customers (our own test purchases), so a log-only run on main would have moved the team's REVENUE issues to Express
- Now only issues whose Dev Source is Community can move to Express; reuses the Source the project manager sets, no separate team list
- The workflow is paused until this merges; it will be re-enabled afterwards

Dry-run locally on 72 hours of issues with every author treated as a customer: 69 Community issues would move, no team-authored ones.

gist.headline: Express takes the community lane
gist.blurb: The Express queue checks the Community label on the project board before waving an issue through. Team issues stay in their own lane.
gist.summary: Express-priority selection uses the project manager's Dev Source = Community field to route community issues while excluding team-authored issues.
gist.impact: In a 72-hour dry run, 69 Community issues qualified for Express and no team-authored issues did.
gist.visual_concept: Depict GitHub issue triage as a cozy garden path: Polli guides Community-tagged issue cards toward a small Express sign, while team issue cards remain on a separate path. A CRT monitor robot helps sort the cards; the project board's Dev Source field is the visual cue.
gist.image_prompt: In a cozy pixel art garden, a CRT monitor robot sorts tiny issue cards marked 'Community' toward an 'Express' sign while Polli, wearing a tiny mail-carrier cap, guides the way beside lime green (#ecf874) code-plants. The main character is a cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body and dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks on cheeks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings. She should be small-to-medium sized within the scene, sharing the frame with other elements — never oversized or dominating the image. Strictly pixel art style, never realistic. Cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes, with a warm cream background and dark purple (#110518) outlines.
